title: Impact of US-China Trade War on Singapore
what_it_is: Impact of US-China Trade War on Singapore

sections.label: US-China trade war impact questions
sections.summary: Questions ask the Minister for Trade and Industry about the US-China trade war's impact on Singapore, workers, consumers, free trade norms and strategy.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry with the ongoing trade war between the US and China (a) what is the impact on Singapore; (b) how will this affect Singapore workers, employment prospects and consumers at large both in the short term and in the long term; (c) whether the US' shift towards protectionist trade affects the global norm of free trade agreements; and (d) what is Singapore's strategy to overcome these challenges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry what are the implications on our economy and industries arising from (i) the increasing trade dispute between the US and the rest of the world, (ii) the current outlook of a multilateralism trading system and (iii) the recent efforts of the EU and China in exploring closer trade links.

sections.label: Exports to US share
sections.summary: Exports of these products to the US are about 0.1% of Singapore's total domestic exports to the world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Our exports of these products to the US account for about 0.1% of our total domestic exports to the world.

sections.label: US-China trade and Singapore GDP
sections.summary: Bilateral US-China trade indirectly contributes 1.1% of Singapore's GDP, and sustained disruption is unwelcome for the region.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: On the whole, bilateral trade between the US and China indirectly contributes to 1.1% of Singapore’s gross domestic product, and any sustained disruption is unwelcome for the region.

sections.label: Tipping point macro-economic change
sections.summary: If measures trigger a sharp sustained fall in global confidence or tighter liquidity, the macro-economic environment will fundamentally change.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Should these measures reach a tipping point that triggers a sharp and sustained fall in global business and consumer confidence, or a tightening of global liquidity conditions, the macro-economic environment will fundamentally change.

sections.label: CPTPP signing and RCEP efforts
sections.summary: The CPTPP signing in March demonstrates commitment to trade liberalisation and regional integration, while ASEAN and FTA partners press on with RCEP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The signing of the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP) in March this year is a tangible demonstration of the parties’ commitment to the collective goals of greater trade liberalisation and regional integration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: ASEAN and our FTA partners are also pressing on with efforts to reach substantive conclusion of the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP).

sections.label: FTAs, companies and multilateral trading
sections.summary: With FTAs, companies can seek new opportunities from trade linkages and supply chains, while Singapore works with partners to uphold rules-based multilateral trade.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: With the FTAs in place, our companies are better positioned to seek out and benefit from new opportunities arising from new trade linkages and supply chains that are formed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We will continue to work with all like-minded partners to uphold a rules-based multilateral trading system, and work towards greater regional integration which is the best way of maximising opportunities for our companies and supporting job creation for Singaporeans.
